summary: Streaming chat responses disconnect mid-generation (SSE/WebSocket) during high-latency period
description: Issue summary: Customer reports streaming chat responses (SSE and WebSocket) disconnecting or stalling mid-generation. Impact: user-visible partial responses and failed assistant turns for interactive chat, leading to degraded UX and increased retry traffic. Environment: production (us-west) on NovaDocs' enterprise dedicated capacity. Observed during a period of increased end-to-end latency and elevated token generation timeouts.
impact: Customers experience mid-generation disconnects or stalls for streaming chat. Affected flows: real-time assistant UIs, live collaboration features. Reports show ~15-20% of streaming requests failing to complete during peak windows; higher on long-context requests.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Using NovaDocs prod account, start a WebSocket streaming chat session to /v1/streams/chat.connect with redwood-open-7b pinned.
2) Send a prompt with multi-turn context (~1.5-2k tokens) that triggers long-generation (>2s token intervals).
3) Observe that after ~8-30s into generation the connection either closes with a 1006/502 or the stream stalls and no more tokens are emitted.
4) Repeat during peak traffic window (approx 17:00-18:30 PST) to match reported failure rate.
5) Alternative reproduction: use SSE endpoint /v1/streams/chat with same prompt and observe 'event: done' never emitted and client receives stalled stream until connection timeout.
Notes: problem frequency increases with longer output lengths and when the serving node is handling multiple concurrent streaming sessions.

comments: 2026-02-20 - Customer (Liam O'Neal, NovaDocs): 'We're seeing sessions return half answers and then disconnect. This is impacting our live editor - can you advise?'

2026-02-20 - Support (Ava Chen): 'Thanks Liam — we've opened SUP-15722. Can you share a request-id and example timestamp? We've requested request-ids from your team; looking into streaming proxy logs.'

2026-02-20 - SRE (Sofia Martinez): 'Preliminary look at us-west cluster: sustained increase in per-token latency starting ~16:45 PST correlating with a burst of long-context requests. Investigating batch scheduler and proxy timeouts.'

2026-02-21 - Eng (Ravi Patel): 'Observed higher KV cache eviction rates during the window; some batches rebuild repeatedly which balloons per-token latency. Also saw proxy upstream read timeouts. Working on mitigation: increase streaming proxy read timeout and adjust batch rebuild threshold.'
2026-02-22 - Customer (Liam O'Neal, NovaDocs): 'After temporary change (increased proxy timeout) we saw improvement but still occasional stalls on 13b model. Any ETA for fix?'

2026-02-23 - Eng (Ravi Patel): 'Rollout of batch throttling patch started to canary in us-west; early metrics show 60% reduction in stalled streams for redwood-open-7b. Continuing observation and will follow up with PR link.'
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Batch scheduler rebuilds under memory pressure are causing repeated rescheduling and long gaps between token emissions -> leads to proxy/read timeouts on client connections.
Hypothesis 2: Serving-runtime kernel selection for certain long-context sequences produces extreme latency on redwood-neo-13b under current quantization path; leads to per-token delay >1s.
Hypothesis 3: Streaming proxy (nginx/gateway) read_timeout is 10s by default; stalls >10s close connection without graceful error which appears as client 1006.
Correlated signals: elevated KV cache eviction rate, increased batch-queue delays, autoscaler pod startup pressure during the incident window.
temporary_mitigations: 1) Increased streaming proxy upstream read_timeout from 10s -> 45s for affected routes (SSE/WebSocket) — deployed 2026-02-21 03:10 UTC.
2) Pin NovaDocs routes to a lower-concurrency serving pool to reduce noisy neighbor impact (temporary routing policy) — applied 2026-02-21 04:00 UTC.
3) Recommended customer-side client retry backoff and idempotent resume where possible.
Observed effect: immediate reduction in hard disconnects but some stalls persisted for 13b model requests.
resolution: Work in progress: batch scheduler patch to avoid repeated rebuilds under partial eviction (serving-runtime PR #2421) is being canaried in us-west (started 2026-02-23).
Post-rollout remedial steps: monitor per-token latency and stalled-stream rate for 48h, if stable then backfill proxy timeout to a safer default and remove emergency routing.
Long-term: improve kernel fallback for redwood-neo-13b quantized path and add streaming-level SLA telemetry to trigger auto-fallback to smaller model variant on sustained stalls.
Follow-ups assigned: INT-3312 (add streaming-specific synthetic checks), INT-3313 (postmortem & KB article for customers).
next_steps: Continue canary of batch scheduler patch through 2026-02-25 and monitor stalled-stream metric every 2 hours.
If canary stable, promote to all-serving pools and notify NovaDocs of rollback plan for temporary routing.
Create KB entry summarizing client-side best practices for SSE/WebSocket resume and recommended timeouts.
Schedule postmortem and include root-cause analysis of interaction between cache eviction and batch rebuild logic.
